question: The government budget is prepared under which article of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 112**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** government budget is prepared under Article 112** of the Constitution of India.
 
• This **article states that the President must present an annual financial statement, also known as the Union Budget, to both houses of Parliament.**
 
• The statement includes estimated government receipts and expenditures for the financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31.
 
• The budget must also be approved by Parliament. 
 
• **The annual financial statement includes: **
 
 
• Salaries, allowances, and pensions
 
• Judgments, decrees, and awards
 
• Other expenditure declared by Constitution or Parliament
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 109**

 
 
• Provides t**he procedure for the passage of Money Bills in Parliament.**
 
• **States that a Money Bill can only be introduced** in the Lok Sabha and must be sent to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations.
 
• The** Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject a Money B**ill but can suggest recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
 
 
 
• **Article 101**
 
 
• Explains **conditions under which a Member of Parliament (MP) may vacate their seat.**
 
• If** a person is elected to both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha,** or to Parliament and a state legislature, they must vacate one seat.
 
• An MP's seat is also vacated if they are absent for 60 consecutive days without permission.
 
 
 
• **Article 100**
 
 
• Describes the** quorum required for either House of Parliament to conduct business (10% of the total membership).**
 
• **States how voting is conducted in Parliament **and that decisions are usually made by a majority of members present and voting.
 
• Ensures that the functioning of the House is not affected by vacancies.
